name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3370
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.”

clue.text: Prepare cured eel's head to lose weight

indicators.note: to prepare food is to work it over, so the letters are worked into a new order
the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the first letter of eel

explanation.surface: A cook gets cured eel ready, cutting off its head to trim the weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' reads as a kitchen instruction, but it is the signal to rearrange cured plus the head of eel into REDUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce is to slim down, the usual word for shedding pounds on a diet.

clue.text: Name exotic club outside capital of Italian nation

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the word is made strange by reordering
outside means placed around, so the shuffled word wraps the next piece
a capital is a word's initial capital letter, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: rep, short for reputation, is one's good name
taken as written, as anagram fodder
the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A nightclub with an exotic name sits just outside the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is not N here but REP, as in a person's reputation; the rearranged club then goes around the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state governed by elected representatives, one kind of nation.

clue.text: 10 eating bread, perhaps with less butter

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: 10-across is defined as Doc, and DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
rye is one kind of bread, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: The doctor is eating bread, perhaps going easy on the butter for health.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare number in a clue stands for that entry; 10-across is defined as Doc, so the doctor's abbreviation is what eats the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast with less butter on it is drier, and the clue's answer is the variant spelling dryer.

clue.text: City's stylish past

blocks.note: chic means stylish
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A city boasts that its past was a stylish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city in Illinois, on the shore of Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Give a hearing to a scrappy Native American

indicators.note: giving something a hearing means listening to it, so the answer is what the words sound like

blocks.note: scrappy means patchy, uneven in quality; say 'a patchy' out loud

explanation.surface: A judge grants a hearing to a feisty Native American plaintiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrappy' suggests a fighter, but here it means patchy or fragmentary, and 'a patchy' spoken runs together into APACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Indigenous peoples of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Ancient city's ceremonial display at the inauguration of Edward the Second

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
the first letter of Edward
Roman numeral two, as in a monarch's title

explanation.surface: A royal coronation, with pageantry at the crowning of King Edward II.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward the Second' reads as one king, but it splits: the inauguration of Edward is just E, and 'the Second' is II.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Carom wildly, captivating young female official

indicators.note: doing something wildly means without control or order, so the letters scatter into a new arrangement
to captivate is literally to take captive, holding the other piece inside

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A wild billiards shot charms a young woman who is an official.
explanation.walkthrough: A carom is a billiards shot in which the ball rebounds; here it is only letters to be rearranged around MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissar was a Communist Party functionary, a political official in the Soviet system.

clue.text: Company in desperate need to make something hard to read

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
desperate suggests frantic disorder, so the word that follows is jumbled

blocks.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A firm in dire straits scrambles its papers to hide them.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message is to put it in cipher, so that it cannot be read without the key.

clue.text: Gets up to embrace beginning of natural hair treatments

indicators.note: embracing someone puts your arms around them, so one piece wraps the other
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: rises means gets up, out of bed or from a seat
the first letter of natural

explanation.surface: Someone gets up in the morning and turns to natural hair products.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a hair tint or conditioner washed through the hair, a common salon treatment.

clue.text: Certain cubist has nightmares

indicators.note: has means contains, so the answer sits inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A particular Cubist painter is plagued by bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: The cubist tempts a search for Braque or Picasso, but the answer is lying in plain sight across certain and cubist.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus was a demon thought to lie on sleepers, and so a word for a nightmare or oppressive dream; this is the plural.

clue.text: Doc [that's what it says here] is involved in any hip replacement

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a replacement puts things in new positions, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: sic is the Latin tag editors use to mean 'this is what the original says'
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A surgeon is part of any hip replacement operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is the clue for SIC, which editors print in square brackets. Doc is also one of the Seven Dwarfs, the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is an informal word for a doctor, and a physician is a medical doctor.

clue.text: Lead soprano role in a Puccini opera about an ape

blocks.clueFragment: Lead soprano role in a Puccini opera
blocks.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
c. is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A soprano sings the lead in a Puccini opera whose plot concerns an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase looks like the definition, inviting TOSCA or MANON, but it only builds MIMI; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape, in the sense of someone who copies others, is a mimic.

clue.text: Rumba dancing in Myanmar

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: People are doing the rumba in Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, the country renamed in 1989.

clue.text: Bend down if I'd sounded dopey

indicators.note: sounded means spoken out, so the answer matches the words as they are pronounced

blocks.note: to stoop is to bend down; run 'stoop if I'd' together and it is a single word

explanation.surface: Someone says they would have bent down if only they had sounded less dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dopey is also one of the Seven Dwarfs, part of the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means dazed or drowsy, as stupefied describes someone dulled by drugs or shock.

clue.text: Happy drummer loses head, takes an excessive amount of drugs, and trips out when eating pie filling

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the name is cut off
out in the sense of disordered or awry, so the word before it is rearranged
eating takes something in, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
a filling is what is in the middle, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

blocks.clueFragment: takes an excessive amount of drugs
blocks.note: ODs, short for overdoses, means takes too much of a drug
taken as written, as anagram fodder
the middle letter of pie

explanation.surface: A cheerful drummer overdoes the drugs and has hallucinations while eating pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's drugs and trips are all wordplay: Ringo minus R, then ODS, then trips rearranged around the I. Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in good spirits is an idiom for being cheerful and upbeat.

clue.text: It's not likely the female principle, separating thousands, is turning to vapor

indicators.note: to separate two things you put something between them, so the pieces go into the gap

blocks.note: G, for grand, is American slang for a thousand dollars; plural, so two
'as if!' is a scornful way of saying that is not likely
yin is the female principle in Chinese philosophy, paired with yang

explanation.surface: A philosophical line about the female principle being unlikely, separating thousands, as it evaporates.
explanation.walkthrough: Both inner pieces sit between the two thousands, one G at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasify is to convert into gas, so gasifying is the process of turning into vapor.

clue.text: Rose accepts Biden's ascent as a personal irritant

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent reads the word from bottom to top, back to front
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Pete Rose is a famous American baseball player
Joe Biden was then US vice president, informally the veep

explanation.surface: Pete Rose tolerates Joe Biden's rise as a personal annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a flower or a past tense, but it is the surname of the baseball star Pete Rose. The answer runs on into 26-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet peeve is an idiom for a particular thing that annoys someone more than it should.

clue.text: I really make an effort to limit Western city's fetishism

indicators.note: limiting something hems it in on both sides, so the phrase surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: 'I do try' is an emphatic way of saying I really make an effort
LA is Los Angeles, a city in the American West

explanation.surface: Someone protests they really try to keep a Western city's obsessions in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object worshipped for supposed magical power, so fetishism is a kind of idol worship.

clue.text: Grumpy, brusque, and embarrassed about Arizona city

blocks.note: short means curt or brusque in manner
Tempe is a city in Arizona, near Phoenix
red-faced, as when embarrassed

explanation.surface: A grumpy, curt person is embarrassed about some Arizona city.
explanation.walkthrough: Being red about Tempe is read as Tempe followed by red, so the city comes first. Grumpy is one of the Seven Dwarfs, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone grumpy is irritable, and short-tempered means quick to anger.

clue.text: "Ring is ring" is wrong, for starters

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so the quoted words are rearranged

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pedant objects that saying 'ring is ring' is a bad way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted sentence looks like a statement being judged, but its first word is the letter O and the rest is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are beginnings, the points where things start.

clue.text: That group's clothing is an alternative to 17

indicators.note: clothing covers what is inside it, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: them refers to that group of people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribe's style of dress is offered as a substitute for another custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is IDOLATRY, the worship of idols; the answer is belief in a god instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism, belief in a single god or gods, is the doctrine set against worshipping idols.

clue.text: Bury Benjamin and Thomas, with the former's head at the latter's foot

indicators.text: with the former's head at the latter's foot
indicators.note: the first name's opening letter is taken off its front and set down at the very end, after the second name

blocks.note: Ben is short for Benjamin
Tom is short for Thomas

explanation.surface: An instruction for burying two men, Benjamin and Thomas, head to foot.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry Ben sits above Tom, so moving Ben's head to Tom's foot sends the B to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, that is, to bury it.

clue.text: Common accompaniment for film erotica enthralling crooked cop

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the first piece holds the second inside
crooked means bent out of shape, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: porn is a short word for erotica
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The usual extra with an erotic film is a corrupt policeman held spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film erotica' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at film and erotica starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is the snack traditionally eaten while watching a movie.

clue.text: You may have to have it when buying alcohol or mixing acid on road

definitions.text: You may have to have it when buying alcohol

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A warning about the paperwork needed to buy liquor, or to mix chemicals on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellers of alcohol must check age, so buyers who look young are asked for identification such as an ID card.

clue.text: Alien I find deft and bashful

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the letters take on an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone says they find an alien both skilful and shy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bashful is one of the Seven Dwarfs, part of the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffident means lacking self-confidence, which is the same shyness as bashful.

clue.text: Small dog with one large student

blocks.note: a pup is a young, small dog
the Roman numeral for one
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A tiny dog accompanies one big schoolkid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner at a school, another word for a student.

clue.text: See 16
Excuse tabloid bait, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions keeps the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

blocks.note: every second letter of these two words, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Someone pleads they took the tabloid bait without weighing the risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring the odds' sounds like recklessness, but it means dropping the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, and informally any excuse.

clue.text: Consequently, a set of letters associated with 6 days of penitence makes you sleepy

blocks.note: so means therefore, consequently

blocks.clueFragment: a set of letters associated with 6
blocks.note: on a telephone keypad the 6 key carries the letters M, N and O
Lent is the Christian season of fasting and penitence

explanation.surface: Six days of penance leave a person drowsy as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 days' reads as a span of time, but the 6 is a phone key's letters. Sleepy is one of the Seven Dwarfs, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, inclined to fall asleep.

clue.text: Appreciate joke, when Jack leaves a summary

indicators.note: Jack is J in card notation, and its leaving means that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking or appreciating it
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A listener enjoys a joke once Jack has left, and someone sums it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed version of longer material, such as a digest of the news.

clue.text: Yes, Zen paradoxically… wait! This word was supposed to be in a clue, not in the diagram!

definitions.text: This word was supposed to be in a clue, not in the diagram

indicators.note: paradoxically means contrary to expectation, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
surface padding: the setters interrupting themselves, giving no letters

explanation.surface: A Zen paradox interrupted by the setters noticing a blunder in their own puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the Seven Dwarfs (Doc, Dopey, Happy, Grumpy, Bashful, Sleepy) are definitions in other clues; this one landed in the grid instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The other six dwarfs from Snow White are clue definitions, so the seventh dwarf belongs in a clue too.
